source: Every UDP/5678 frame the hub.ts station received on the hub segment (CHRs 7.26beta5 x2, 7.17.2, 7.18.2, 7.20.8, 6.49.23), from the start of requests-fresh.json to the end of the session, 2026-11-16. The station logs what it receives, not what it sends; t is ms since the hub process started. requests-fresh.json and requests-main-run2.json `sends` and `anchors` below use that clock. running-7.26beta5.json and ipv6-7.17-7.26beta5.json do not: their `announcements[].t` are offsets from each step's start, and the step's hub-clock start was not recorded. Match those by payloadHex instead. requests-forms.json and requests-main-run1.json came from an earlier hub process with its own clock.

anchors.z9 sequences (seq.ts, ad hoc): between t≈95000 and t=198085: from fresh MACs 02:4d:4e:44:5a:01/02 and from the station: [00000000 then, 1 s after its replies, 000000000000000000], [000000000000000000 alone], [00000000, 000000000000000000, 000000000006000000, 0000000000 each 5 s apart]; only the 00000000 sends drew replies
anchors.interval 1h→2h on obs,sub,r717,r718,r720: set at t=349917, 350002, 350080, 350163, 350248; one triggered announcement each, 1.3–2.2 s later, then nothing for 75 s
anchors.interval 2h→10s, then 10s→1h: 10s set at t≈448186–448506 (obs first); triggered announcements at t≈448545–450343, then no 10 s periodics; 1h set at t≈488599–488928, triggered announcements at t≈489287–490433, then nothing for 40 s
anchors.6.49.23 reboots: boot announcement header 00000000 (IPv4 only) at t=1080239 (ipv6 package disabled) and t=1140553 (enabled); with the package enabled the next announcement went out on IPv4 and IPv6 with TLV 14 = 01
